rule: Skip one-time comparisons; record exact source and concrete why. Do not exclude a reusable collocation/idiom or a source with unresolved grammar, antecedent, owner or source-order questions.
method: Independently read all 39 exact source examples, meanings and current decision rows; confirmed each source and decision raw hash still matches B’s report.
Compared candidate cores with existing/selected owner meanings and target patterns; complete-source detector matches alone are insufficient and no source was automatically aliased.
Accepted exclusion only for the exact source-specific image or aphorism, never as rejection of a separate conventional subphrase. Rejected exclusions remain current holds.

ownerOrSourceOrderHighlights.issue: same appearance-versus-substance sense, but later owner and awkward source form; migration/naturalness gate
same action-versus-speech sense, but later owner; migration and bounded form gate
earlier spark owners overlap trigger/growth aspects; assess exact fire-image source before any merge
buried-under construction present, but abstract curiosity-obscured sense differs from person overwhelmed by chores

externalUsageChecks.finding: be awake to something can mean know about it; does not alone prove the whole source is a course unit
in disguise is a productive phrase for an apparent versus real nature; owner110 blessing-in-disguise is narrower

rows.exactSourceSentence: A phone call gives the moment more heart than a short post.
rows.sourceQuestion: How do people share good news?
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: Adds warmth and emotional meaning; heart is figurative.
rows.reason: The call-versus-short-post comparison supplies the warmth claim; gives the moment more heart is tailored to that single moment. Excluding this exact comparison does not rule out general heart collocations.

rows.exactSourceSentence: The story was passed hand to hand, heart to heart.
rows.expression: passed hand to hand, heart to heart
rows.sourceQuestion: How do people share good news?
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: Shared privately and personally; a paired body-part image.
rows.reason: Hand to hand, heart to heart is a paired rhyme for this story handoff. Heart-to-heart conversation has a separate established sense, so the whole pair is not a reusable target here.

rows.exactSourceSentence: A rumour can move at the speed of a thumb swipe.
rows.expression: at the speed of a thumb swipe
rows.sourceQuestion: What is the difference between new media and old media?
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: Very quickly in a phone-based setting; a contemporary speed image.
rows.reason: At the speed of a thumb swipe is a newly coined speed image tied to phone rumours; retaining the general at-the-speed-of pattern would not preserve this source-specific comparison.

rows.exactSourceSentence: Even accurate facts can be arranged so the angle may still tilt.
rows.sourceQuestion: Do you think the contents in the newspapers are reliable?
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: The perspective can lean toward one side; an orientation metaphor.
rows.reason: The angle may still tilt is a bespoke and awkward second spatial image for arranging facts; the complete frame is not a bounded way to teach media bias.

rows.exactSourceSentence: A second report shines a different light on the same picture.
rows.expression: shines a different light on the same picture
rows.sourceQuestion: Do you think the contents in the newspapers are reliable?
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: Offers a different interpretation of the same facts; paired light and picture images.
rows.reason: Shines a different light on can express a transferable reinterpretation; the added same picture may be mixed imagery, but it does not justify excluding the reusable light-on core. Keep held for grammar and comparison with owners 2278/4652.
rows.sourceOrderOrOwnerIssue: Owners 2278 shed light on and 4652 shine a light on teach explanation/visibility, not automatically the same changed-interpretation sense; 2278 is earlier and 4652 later.

rows.exactSourceSentence: We should stay awake to the world without reading every alert.
rows.sourceQuestion: Do you think it's necessary for people to watch foreign news?
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: Remain aware of events beyond oneself; wakefulness is figurative.
rows.reason: Be awake to something is an attested awareness construction, and this source may use it for awareness of wider events. Keep held while testing the exact awake-to-the-world grammar and six decisions.
rows.sourceOrderOrOwnerIssue: No selected full-source detector match; this is a possible new bounded collocation, not a ready alias.

rows.exactSourceSentence: News often finds them while they browse for entertainment.
rows.sourceQuestion: How has social media changed how we consume news?
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: People encounter news without searching; a personification.
rows.reason: News finds them describes incidental discovery while browsing; this subject-verb pattern can recur across feeds and audiences, so one-off exclusion is premature. Test contrast with active news seeking.
rows.sourceOrderOrOwnerIssue: No current owner/complete-source detector match identified.

rows.exactSourceSentence: Online, the reaction arrives before the reporting.
rows.sourceQuestion: How has social media changed how we consume news?
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: Opinions spread before verified facts; an arrival metaphor.
rows.reason: Reaction arrives before the reporting personifies two processes to make one temporal comparison; the sentence states a media observation rather than a reusable target phrase.

rows.exactSourceSentence: Children are like little mirrors when they copy our tone.
rows.sourceQuestion: For parents, what is important when bringing up their children?
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: Children reflect adults' habits and attitudes; a mirror simile.
rows.reason: Children are like little mirrors when they copy our tone is an explicit analogy for this imitation example; neither little mirrors nor the whole simile supplies a distinct assessable idiom.

rows.exactSourceSentence: In our family, love is the foundation of every rule.
rows.sourceQuestion: Do you think mothers and fathers have different roles to play in bringing up a child?
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: Care is the basic support of parenting; a building metaphor.
rows.reason: X is the foundation of Y is a reusable support metaphor. Love grounding family rules may be compositional, but it warrants a foundation-owner and seven-decision comparison before exclusion.
rows.sourceOrderOrOwnerIssue: Earlier owners 1119 and 1911 teach lay/build foundations in different grammar; neither is an automatic alias.

rows.exactSourceSentence: Discipline should never teach fear as a language of love.
rows.expression: fear as a language of love
rows.sourceQuestion: Do you think hitting children is sometimes necessary for discipline?
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: Treating frightening punishment as if it communicates care; a pointed language metaphor.
rows.reason: Fear as a language of love is a pointed one-time critique of frightening discipline; it does not teach the established love-language term in its ordinary sense.

rows.exactSourceSentence: The diet is too strict if every biscuit feels like a moral crisis.
rows.expression: every biscuit feels like a moral crisis
rows.sourceQuestion: Do you think sweets are a good thing to reward children with?
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: Treating an ordinary treat as a serious ethical issue; a deliberately exaggerated comparison.
rows.reason: Every biscuit feels like a moral crisis deliberately exaggerates one restrictive diet; moral crisis itself means a real ethical dilemma and should not be taught from the biscuit hyperbole.

rows.exactSourceSentence: Family gatherings can be emotional bookmarks in life.
rows.sourceQuestion: When do people usually have parties in your country?
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: Celebrations that help people remember meaningful periods; a book metaphor.
rows.reason: Emotional bookmarks in life is a coined book image for these family gatherings; a generic bookmark metaphor would need a different source and decision.

rows.exactSourceSentence: The campaign risks dressing the window while the house still needs repair.
rows.expression: dressing the window while the house still needs repair
rows.sourceQuestion: Why do some people think that national celebrations are a waste of government money? Do you agree or disagree with this view? Why?
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: Improving appearances while ignoring serious problems; an extended house metaphor.
rows.reason: The appearance-versus-needed-repair judgment is the same family as window dressing. The source form dressing the window may be awkward, but keep it held for source-naturalness and owner comparison rather than excluding it.
rows.sourceOrderOrOwnerIssue: Selected owner4700 window dressing is later than source2962; direct alias-new would violate earliest-source ordering without an ownership migration.

rows.exactSourceSentence: At a small gathering, joy often lands more deeply.
rows.sourceQuestion: How important is it to celebrate important events with a group of people?
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: Shared happiness can feel more meaningful; landing is figurative.
rows.reason: Joy lands more deeply may be an instance of the reusable figurative land meaning have an emotional effect; the comparative is thin, but excluding it before a naturalness/sense check would be premature.
rows.sourceOrderOrOwnerIssue: No complete-source owner detector match; no ready alias.

rows.exactSourceSentence: Life runs on small choices more than grand plans.
rows.sourceQuestion: What decisions do people generally make in their daily life?
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: Daily life depends on many modest decisions; a machine metaphor.
rows.reason: Runs on is productive dependence/fuel language; life depending on small choices is a reusable construction even if this sentence is aphoristic. Test positive and negative dependence cases before exclusion.
rows.sourceOrderOrOwnerIssue: Earlier owners1400 and1651 use narrower run-on complements. A bounded owner expansion is possible only after sense and assessment review.

rows.exactSourceSentence: For lunch plans, solo decisions often feel lighter.
rows.sourceQuestion: Which is easier, making a decision by oneself or making a decision after a group discussion?
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: Individual decisions can feel less burdensome; weight is figurative.
rows.reason: Feel lighter is a familiar figurative reduction-of-burden collocation; the lunch example may be narrow, but solo versus group decision weight can transfer. Keep held for course-value review.
rows.sourceOrderOrOwnerIssue: No complete-source owner detector match; no ready alias.

rows.exactSourceSentence: Her caution was less about weakness and more about weight.
rows.expression: less about weakness and more about weight
rows.sourceQuestion: Why do middle-aged people tend to second-guess their decisions?
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: Hesitation reflects responsibility rather than frailty; weight is figurative.
rows.reason: Less about X and more about Y is a reusable corrective discourse pattern; weakness versus responsibility/weight is one use. Hold for a bounded contrast and six distinct decisions, rather than classing the entire construction as one-off.
rows.sourceOrderOrOwnerIssue: No complete-source owner detector match; no ready alias.

rows.exactSourceSentence: Adulthood includes carrying that freedom responsibly.
rows.sourceQuestion: Should people consider the consequences of their decisions that impact others, or only think of themselves?
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: Using independence with care for consequences; a weight metaphor.
rows.reason: Carrying that freedom responsibly is a bespoke adulthood burden image. The source teaches responsibility in a claim, not a bounded carry-freedom expression.

rows.exactSourceSentence: The effects of a major choice rarely stay in one neat corner.
rows.sourceQuestion: Should people consider the consequences of their decisions that impact others, or only think of themselves?
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: Remain limited to one person's life or one area; a spatial image.
rows.reason: Effects staying in one neat corner is an ad hoc spatial image for spillover from a major choice; a general consequence-crossing-boundaries lesson would change the source unit.

rows.exactSourceSentence: Curiosity can be buried under the noise of everyday life.
rows.expression: buried under the noise of everyday life
rows.sourceQuestion: Do you think adults can have lots of imagination?
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: Hidden by routine demands; burial and noise imagery.
rows.reason: Buried under is reusable figurative language; the source describes curiosity obscured by daily-life noise. It needs a naturalness and sense comparison, not a one-off exclusion.
rows.sourceOrderOrOwnerIssue: Earlier owner1682 buried under chores describes a person overwhelmed by tasks; this source has an abstract subject obscured by noise, so not a direct alias.

rows.exactSourceSentence: Her creative side wakes up again when she paints.
rows.sourceQuestion: Do you think adults can have lots of imagination?
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: Becomes active after a dormant period; wakefulness is figurative.
rows.reason: The creative side wakes up again can express dormant ability reactivating across settings. The phrasal verb is transferable; assess its figurative boundary before exclusion.
rows.sourceOrderOrOwnerIssue: No selected full-source target match; no ready alias.

rows.exactSourceSentence: The proposal began with a first leap of thought.
rows.sourceQuestion: Do you think imagination is necessary for scientists?
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: An initial imaginative jump beyond known facts; a movement metaphor.
rows.reason: First leap of thought is a one-time movement image for an early idea; no stable phrase or distinct seven-step decision follows from the full wording.

rows.exactSourceSentence: In design, imagination is the engine under the bonnet.
rows.sourceQuestion: What kind of jobs need imagination?
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: The essential driving force behind work; a vehicle metaphor.
rows.reason: Engine under the bonnet is a potentially reusable underlying-driver metaphor despite the bespoke design sentence. Verify natural British usage and distinction from engine-room roles before excluding it.
rows.sourceOrderOrOwnerIssue: Selected owner3594 engine room of concerns a producing institution/team, not imagination as an underlying force.

rows.exactSourceSentence: Creative thinking matters when the obvious route leads nowhere.
rows.sourceQuestion: What kind of jobs need imagination?
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: A familiar solution fails; a road metaphor.
rows.reason: Leads nowhere is a reusable failure-of-route/result construction. The creative-thinking sentence gives one case, not evidence that the expression itself is one-off.
rows.sourceOrderOrOwnerIssue: No complete-source owner detector match; potential new bounded lesson, not a ready alias.

rows.exactSourceSentence: The old claim looked weaker under a brighter light.
rows.sourceQuestion: Why do people change their opinion?
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: Examined with clearer evidence; a light metaphor.
rows.reason: Under a brighter light may mean reassessment with clearer evidence; the source form is uncertain but could connect to light-on language. Naturalness and sense must be resolved before exclusion.
rows.sourceOrderOrOwnerIssue: Owners2278/4652 concern making facts clear or visible; neither automatically owns this retrospective re-evaluation.

rows.exactSourceSentence: When plans fail, friends may calm the storm.
rows.sourceQuestion: Who do young people turn to for advice?
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: Friends can ease immediate emotional distress; a weather metaphor.
rows.reason: Calm the storm can be a transferable crisis/conflict metaphor; friends easing a failed plan is one context. Confirm conventionality and target boundaries before excluding it.
rows.sourceOrderOrOwnerIssue: No complete-source owner detector match; no ready alias.

rows.exactSourceSentence: Opinion should not blow about like a weather vane.
rows.expression: blow about like a weather vane
rows.sourceQuestion: Is changing opinions good for society?
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: Change direction with every pressure; a weather-vane simile.
rows.reason: Blow about like a weather vane is an awkward explicit simile for shifting opinion; a prior standalone draft was withdrawn rather than silently normalizing the source to a different weather-vane idiom.
rows.sourceOrderOrOwnerIssue: Earlier exploratory 3123 weather-vane draft was withheld after the naturalness gate; no selected owner.

rows.exactSourceSentence: A good institution can rethink without losing its balance.
rows.sourceQuestion: Is changing opinions good for society?
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: Revise views while keeping stable judgement; a balance metaphor.
rows.reason: Without losing its balance is productive figurative judgment/stability language; institutional rethinking may be one use. Keep held for naturalness and stable decision contrasts.
rows.sourceOrderOrOwnerIssue: No complete-source owner detector match; no ready alias.

rows.exactSourceSentence: Patience is a bit like a muscle in long queues.
rows.expression: patience is a bit like a muscle
rows.sourceQuestion: Who behaves better when waiting, children or adults?
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: Patience improves with practice; a muscle simile.
rows.reason: Patience is a bit like a muscle in long queues is an explicit single-domain teaching analogy, not an idiomatic target with six distinct assessed uses. The exact repeat 3170 should receive the same disposition.

rows.exactSourceSentence: Young children often wear their impatience on the outside.
rows.expression: wear their impatience on the outside
rows.sourceQuestion: Who behaves better when waiting, children or adults?
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: Show impatience openly; a clothing metaphor.
rows.reason: Wear their impatience on the outside is a one-off and nonstandard clothing image. It is not the established wear-your-heart-on-your-sleeve idiom.

rows.exactSourceSentence: Waiting your turn can be discipline in disguise.
rows.sourceQuestion: What are the positive and negative effects of waiting on society?
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: A useful lesson hidden in an unpleasant activity; a fixed disguise metaphor.
rows.reason: In disguise is an established phrase for a thing that is really another kind of thing. The waiting-turn sentence may be awkward, but the reusable construction cannot be dismissed as a nonce comparison.
rows.sourceOrderOrOwnerIssue: Earlier owner110 a blessing in disguise teaches an unexpectedly good outcome; this discipline-in-disguise source is a different hidden-quality claim, not a direct alias.

rows.exactSourceSentence: Patience is a bit like a muscle in long queues.
rows.expression: patience is a bit like a muscle
rows.sourceQuestion: Do you think it is possible to teach people to be more patient?
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: Patience improves with practice; a muscle simile.
rows.reason: Exact repeat of 3133; the same patience-as-muscle analogy has no separate lexical or seven-decision course unit and should share the source-specific disposition.
rows.sourceOrderOrOwnerIssue: Exact repeated source of 3133; both proposed exclusions must be considered together.

rows.exactSourceSentence: A daily inconvenience became the spark that lights the fire of innovation.
rows.expression: the spark that lights the fire of innovation
rows.sourceQuestion: Some people believe that impatience helps the development of technology. Do you agree with that? Why do you think so?
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: A small frustration can begin major invention; an extended fire metaphor.
rows.reason: Spark is a reusable trigger metaphor for an idea or activity; the full fire image is extended, but the source may support a bounded initiating-spark decision. Keep held for owner comparison.
rows.sourceOrderOrOwnerIssue: Earlier owners1138 act like a spark and1173 light the spark teach starting interest/ideas; owner1407 concerns growing an existing spark. Source3181 may fit the first pair after exact-form assessment.

rows.exactSourceSentence: Good engineers are impatient with the problem, but patient with the solution.
rows.expression: impatient with the problem, but patient with the solution
rows.sourceQuestion: Some people believe that impatience helps the development of technology. Do you agree with that? Why do you think so?
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: Urgently seek improvement while carefully developing it; a balanced contrast.
rows.reason: Impatient with the problem, but patient with the solution is a crafted balanced maxim about engineers, not one complete reusable expression; the two adjectives are ordinary productive language.

rows.exactSourceSentence: A close friend can offer the close-up shot on daily pressure.
rows.sourceQuestion: Whose advice do you follow more, your parents' or your friends' advice?
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: A perspective focused on immediate detail; a camera metaphor.
rows.reason: Offer the close-up shot on daily pressure applies camera terminology awkwardly to a friend’s perspective; the whole comparison is source-specific and not a natural standalone target.

rows.exactSourceSentence: Mistakes can be hard teachers for new managers.
rows.sourceQuestion: What can we learn from our mistakes?
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: Errors teach valuable but painful lessons; a personification.
rows.reason: Mistakes can be hard teachers is a natural, potentially reusable learning-from-error metaphor. A seven-step unit may still fail, but that must be tested rather than treating it as an automatically disposable one-off.
rows.sourceOrderOrOwnerIssue: No complete-source owner detector match; no ready alias.

rows.exactSourceSentence: Practice can sharpen the tools inside it, especially careful reasoning.
rows.sourceQuestion: What do children learn from teachers and parents?
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: Improve a child's mental abilities; a tool-and-blade metaphor.
rows.reason: The antecedent of it in sharpen the tools inside it is unresolved. This ambiguity blocks a reliable source sense, so the row must remain held rather than receive a one-time exclusion now.
rows.sourceOrderOrOwnerIssue: No complete-source owner detector match; antecedent resolution precedes any owner test.

rows.exactSourceSentence: At work, character is shown in actions, not just in speeches.
rows.expression: character is shown in actions, not just in speeches
rows.sourceQuestion: What do children learn from teachers and parents?
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: A concise contrast between behaviour and words; a reusable moral reasoning pattern.
rows.reason: The actions-versus-speeches contrast expresses the same general behavior-over-promises decision as an existing selected idiom. Preserve it as a potential source-order owner issue, not a one-off exclusion.
rows.sourceOrderOrOwnerIssue: Selected owner4444 actions can sometimes speak louder than words is later than source3267. Direct alias-new requires earliest-source ownership resolution and bounded form review.

limits: Accept is a recommendation for exact-source one-time exclusion, not an applied exclusion, publication approval or human sign-off.
Reject means retain hold while the stated naturalness, owner or seven-step gate is investigated; it does not approve a new lesson or alias.
